messages:
Sam: heads-up — v4.12.0 roll started 10m ago, deploy-bot flagged a streaming disconnect regression in hosted canary. small but customers hit.

deploy-bot: [AUTOMATED ALERT] canary-hosted / stream-io: p99 connection-reset = +520ms vs baseline, error-rate 0.48% (threshold 0.3%) — suggested: auto-rollback to v4.11.3.

Aisha: seeing aborted streams in logs too. sample: `stream_conn: EOF after 2s` across 3 hosts. Filing request to correlate with http/2 mux change.

Carla: @Sam are dedicated pools impacted? we need to know before flipping rollback for everyone.

Eli: checked dedicated-prod-embeddings and eu-dedicated: no increase in resets. looks isolated to hosted fronting layer (ingress-proxy http/2 mux config).

Sam: ok — deploy-bot suggested auto-rollback but we have a scheduled change window for critical customers (legal notified). I do not want a full auto-rollback without ops ack. holding manual decision.

Marta: recommendation: partial rollback for hosted-api gateway only (pin gateway image to 3.9.1) and keep dedicated unchanged. will that create compatibility churn?

Luis: partial rollback seems safest. we can route 100% hosted traffic to pinned gateway image via traffic-tag `hosted-pin-v3` and keep other routes alone. runbook below.

Carla: please paste exact rollback commands, and who will execute. also craft a short customer blurb.

Eli: rollback commands (gateway control):
```bash
# pin hosted gateway deployment to image 3.9.1
kubectl -n hosted set image deploy/gateway gateway=redwood/gateway:3.9.1 --record
# patch routing to use traffic-tag
redwoodctl routing set --route hosted-api --tag hosted-pin-v3 --percent 100
```

Marta: I'll execute the kubectl step. @Luis can you drive the routing command? I'll be on the bridge.

Luis: ack. starting routing set now. applying gradual 30s step then 100% if no errors.

deploy-bot: action: routing change started by Luis. 30% -> 100% in 3 steps. health-checks running.

Sam: quick checklist for comms: (1) short customer note in /customers/hosted-updates, (2) update release_notes with rollback entry, (3) notify CSMs for top 10 dedicated customers that are unaffected so they don't overreact.

Aisha: draft blurb: "We observed degraded streaming reliability for Hosted API after v4.12.0; we've rolled the Hosted API gateway back to the prior image to restore streaming continuity. No action needed on your side; Dedicated and private deployments are unaffected." happy to post after approval.

Carla: +1. Sam — approve to post?

Sam: approved. Marta go ahead and execute the kubectl step. Luis continue routing. keep me posted every step.

Marta: kubectl applied. pods rolling, two out of three ready.

Luis: routing at 30% -> health ok -> 100% applied. deploy-bot health-checks pass.

deploy-bot: [INFO] hosted gateway pinned to 3.9.1, canary->prod routing at 100%, metrics stabilizing (p99 resets returned to baseline within 2m).

Eli: verified metrics: error-rate back down to 0.08%, p99 reset delta <-10ms. good.

Sam: great. Next steps: 1) update release_notes.md with rollback entry and note cause (http/2 mux change), 2) run a small test sweep with streaming function-calls, 3) open an infra follow-up ticket to revert gateway http/2 changes and re-run canary when ready. I'll ping legal/CSM for customer note.

Marta: posting customer blurb now. link: https://customers.redwood/status/hosted-streaming-2024-rollback

Carla: creating follow-up infra ticket: INFRA-4098 "Investigate http/2 multiplexing change that caused streamed connection resets" and tagging @networking.

Sam: thanks everyone. marking thread resolved when release_notes updated and ticket created. :white_check_mark:
